assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int.
Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
Output contains no Groovy or Spock syntax: no def, where:, expect:, given:, GString interpolation (#variable), Spock assertions (thrown(), old()), or Groovy list literals ([] as Set).
